free_text: The patient is a 65-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 4.53 and a biopsy-proven Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1) prostate adenocarcinoma with high-risk features. MRI revealed a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone, correlating with the clinical T1c stage. Given the high-risk pathological findings and imaging evidence, the management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefits against the risks of progression.
